data.name: Aulea
data.gender_notes: Aulea is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word 'aulos' which means 'shepherd'. In ancient Greece, the name Aulea was given to little girls who were destined to become shepherdesses. This name is rich in symbolism, representing nurturing, care, and protection. The name Aulea carries the meaning “Little shepherdess” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Aulea usually hope their child will grow to embody little shepherdess and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Aulea belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Little shepherdess.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aulea total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Aulea carries a deep cultural significance as it is rooted in ancient Greek history. It symbolizes the simple yet essential role of a shepherd in caring for their flock, keeping them safe and nourished. This name reflects a strong connection to nature and the beauty and peace it brings to our lives.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Aulea lies in its association with the role of a shepherd. In Christian tradition, Jesus is often referred to as the Great Shepherd who guides and protects His people. Aulea is a reminder of the selfless love and care that Jesus demonstrates for us. It calls us to be caregivers, loving and nurturing those around us, just as a shepherd cares for their flock. This name serves as a reminder to be compassionate, compassionate, and present for those in need, spreading love and light in the world.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Aulea was a Roman noblewoman who lived during the late Republic. The name Aulea carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Aulea was a member of the noble Cornelia gens and was the mother of Marcus Licinius Crassus, one of the most powerful men in Rome during the late Republic.
